questions.question: When an older acting face carries a moustache at medium scale, how is the upper-lip/mouth region constructed so the expression stays readable: moustache value contrast against the face, separate visible mouth shape below it, and how much gap?

witnesses.observed: farm (moustache): moustache = darkest face mark (hair value), compact bar; mouth a separate small dark shape BELOW it with a skin gap; nose small darker wedge above. clinic (no facial hair, unlike): mouth sits directly under the nose region. Grey-haired identity can keep light hair while the facial-hair mass separates by value.

producer.if: facial hair covers the mouth region of an ACTING_CUE face
producer.then: facial-hair fill is value-separated from the face plane (contrast >= 2.2) and the mouth is a separate dark shape below it with a visible skin gap, sized for its expression states
producer.falsifier: a source acting face where light facial hair on similar-value skin reads clearly with no gap
producer.counterexample: no facial hair: mouth placed directly under the nose (clinic)
producer.op: engine/authoring/construct.mjs#separateFrom: value-separation op; films/_qual_A/subjects/engineer.mjs#facialHair: moustache fill + mouth geometry
